title: Oncall choreography and stakeholder briefs — Responder handbook
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Overview

This handbook codifies how Redwood responders should move through an incident from first signal to long-term remediation while keeping internal stakeholders and affected customers appropriately informed. It focuses on choreography (who does what when), short-cycle status templates, runbook gating points, and a practical game-day exercise to validate the flow.

Scope

- Applies to all production-impacting incidents for the Redwood inference platform (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Intended audience: oncall responders, incident commanders, engineering leadership, customer success, and communications.
- Not a replacement for service-specific runbooks — it links to those and specifies handoff criteria.

Summary of core principles

1) Fast containment, then measured communication. Avoid premature promises — surface clear facts.
2) Roles and ownership are temporary; focus on resolving and learning.
3) Communicate at predictable cadence and with clear escalation triggers.
4) Use the incident id for all messages: {{INCIDENT_ID}}.

Incident lifecycle and choreography

1) Signal and Triage (0–10 minutes)
   - Alert received by primary oncall.
   - Primary acknowledges within 3 minutes in PagerDuty / Slack channel #incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}}.
   - If severity >= Sev-2, the primary triggers Incident Commander (IC) role.

2) Initial Assessment and Containment (10–30 minutes)
   - IC declares Severity level using the severity matrix below and assigns roles: communications lead, SRE lead, product liaison, customer-success liaison.
   - Quick containment steps executed from a checklist: throttle routes, toggle canary, enable degraded mode, or scale capacity.

3) Stabilization (30–180 minutes)
   - Establish an operational bridge and logging. Ensure tracing and request sampling are at 100% for affected endpoints.
   - IC updates stakeholders every 30 minutes with short status bullets.

4) Recovery and Verification (90–720 minutes)
   - Run pre-defined verification playbooks and synthetic checks.
   - Gradual rollback of temporary mitigations only after verification windows.

5) Post-incident (within 72 hours)
   - Postmortem timeline and owner assignment. Capture action items, severity rationale, and RCA.

Severity classification (summary table)

| Severity | Customer Impact | Examples | Escalation window |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sev-1 | Complete outage for a region or tier | Hosted API down for >5 min | Immediate (0–5 min) |
| Sev-2 | Significant degradation >25% of requests | Latency > 5s for core routes | 5–15 minutes |
| Sev-3 | Minor degradation, partial feature loss | Embeddings slow for some customers | 15–60 minutes |
| Sev-4 | Informational / non-customer affecting | Scheduled backup failed | <24 hours |

Incident roles and responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): overall orchestration, decisive communications, risk tolerance decisions.
- Communications Lead: drafts internal and external messages; coordinates with CS and legal when required.
- Primary Responder / SRE Lead: performs first diagnosis and implements containment.
- Product Liaison: explains user-visible symptoms and prioritizes features affected.
- Postmortem Owner: ensures RCA, action tracking, and verification.

Role handoff checklist (quick, for IC to run)

1. Confirm new IC accepts responsibility in channel.
2. Summarize what’s known and outstanding tasks.
3. Confirm active mitigations and who controls them.

Runbook gating points (where to stop and re-evaluate)

- After every blocking mitigation (e.g., rolling back a deploy), pause 10 minutes and validate traffic and metrics before proceeding.
- If a hypothesis is unconfirmed after 30 minutes, escalate to SRE lead for deeper sampling.
- Any mitigation that impacts customer data or privacy requires immediate legal and security notification.

Communications: cadence, channels, and templates

Channels
- Internal: Slack channel #incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}}, PagerDuty, Pager (phone when urgent), internal status site.
- External: Status Page (status.redwood.ai), Customer Success Slack/Email for high-touch accounts, and public incident notes where applicable.

Cadence
- Initial internal acknowledgement: within 10 minutes.
- IC internal updates: every 30 minutes while active.
- External status updates: every 60 minutes for Sev-1/Sev-2, every 3 hours for Sev-3 as needed, and on resolution.

Internal status template (30s read)

- Subject: [{{INCIDENT_ID}}] Internal Status — t+{{ELAPSED}}
- Severity: Sev-2
- Summary: Short, factual sentence describing impact.
- What we did: bullet list of mitigations applied.
- What we’re doing next: next 30–60 minute actions.
- Owner: Name (Role)

Customer-facing status page template (public)

- Title: Degraded performance for Redwood API ({{REGION}}) — {{INCIDENT_ID}}
- Impact: Brief statement of customer-visible impact.
- Status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigated / Resolved
- ETA: Next update at HH:MM UTC
- Details: Non-technical summary and link to updates.

Example public status message: 

"We are currently investigating degraded performance for the Redwood generation API in {{REGION}}. Some customers may experience increased latency or timeouts. Our engineers have identified a routing regression and are implementing a fix. Next update: in 60 minutes. Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}." 

High-touch customer brief (email)

Subject: [Redwood] Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — Customer impact update

Hi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},

We are investigating an issue impacting the Redwood API in {{REGION}} that may affect request latency and success for your integration. Our oncall SRE team has applied traffic isolation and is working on a fix. We will update you at least hourly until resolved. If you see material impacts to your SLA, reply to this thread and we will escalate prioritization.

Status: Investigating
Estimated next update: HH:MM UTC
Primary contact: {{CS_REP}} ({{CS_EMAIL}})

Thank you for your patience,
The Redwood Incident Team

On-call rotations and handoffs

Rotation model
- Primary oncall rotates weekly. Secondary (backup) rotates on a two-week cadence. Each rotation document in the rota repo lists holiday overrides and escalation contacts.

Handoff checklist (new oncall)
1. Review the active incidents list and open Slack channels.
2. Check the runbook healthboard (Status -> Runbook Health).
3. Confirm contact details for secondary and IC on-call.
4. Perform a brief warm startup: run the canary smoke test locally.

Game-day exercise (quarterly)

Purpose: validate the entire incident choreography, from signal to postmortem, including comms templates and cross-team notifications.

Format (4 hours)
- 0:00–0:15 — Inject: synthetic downstream failure causing API latency.
- 0:15–0:45 — Triage and declare severity.
- 0:45–1:45 — Execute containment plan and send first public status update.
- 1:45–2:30 — Recovery verification and phased mitigation rollback.
- 2:30–4:00 — Postmortem-lite and action assignment.

Success criteria
- Incident acknowledged in <3 minutes.
- First public update sent <60 minutes for Sev-1/2.
- Postmortem owner assigned within 24 hours.

Postmortem and action tracking

- Postmortem must be published within 72 hours of resolution with the following sections: timeline, impact, root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions, verification plan, and preventive controls.
- Actions require an owner, priority (P0,P1,P2), and verification date. Unverified P0/P1s are escalated in the next reliability review.

Metrics, dashboards and SLOs to monitor during incidents

- 99th percentile latency per model route (SLO: 95% <= 1.5s).
- Error rate per route (SLO: < 0.5% errors).
- Token throughput by region and queue depth.
- CPU/GPU utilization on serving fleet.

Operational runbook index (examples)

- Route throttling and rate-limit failover: link to runbook (Service: route-proxy)
- Model fallback / downgrade procedure: link to runbook (Service: model-router)
- Spot instance scaling rollback: link to runbook (Service: autoscaler)
- Data-plane circuit breaker reset: link to runbook (Service: ingress-controller)

Appendix: Quick reference templates

CLI example: acknowledge an incident in PagerDuty\
```
pagerduty incidents acknowledge --id {{INCIDENT_ID}} --note "Acknowledged by Primary oncall: {{NAME}}"
```

Emergency escalation matrix (short)
- After 10 minutes with no progress on a Sev-1: contact SRE Director and Head of Product.
- Any incident with data-exfiltration indicators: halt mitigations and notify Security immediately.

Retention of incident artifacts
- All incident channels and logs are preserved for 90 days in the incident archive bucket. Postmortems are retained indefinitely in Confluence.

How to use this handbook
- Bookmark this page and link service-specific runbooks into the Operational runbook index.
- For deviations to this process (e.g., regulatory-required timelines for a Private deployment), coordinate with the Security and Legal teams and mark the incident confidentiality as "restricted".

Revision history
- 2024-03-15: Initial published draft.
- 2025-07-07: Added game-day cadence and updated escalation matrix.
- 2026-01-18: Clarified runbook gating and public communication cadence.
